title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: morphisms X --f--> S --> T. On Ω•_{X/T} there is the Koszul filtration by the images of f*Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗ Ω•_{X/T}[-p]. On the previous page Grothendieck uses the projection formula to identify the graded pieces (eq. 3): Gr^p Rf_*Ω•_{X/T} ≅ Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω•_{X/S}[-p]. The connecting maps d_1 of the filtered object give morphisms (6) Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω•_{X/S} → Ω^{p+1}_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω•_{X/S}, with d_1∘d_1 = 0. For p = 0 this is the Gauss–Manin connection.

On this page:
(8) Taking cohomology sheaves H^q gives maps H^q(Ω^p ⊗^L Rf_*Ω•_{X/S}) → H^q(Ω^{p+1} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω•_{X/S}).
(8') When Ω^1_{S/T} is flat (so all Ω^p_{S/T} are flat), these become Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗ R^q f_*Ω•_{X/S} → Ω^{p+1}_{S/T} ⊗ R^q f_*Ω•_{X/S}. In degree p = 0 this is an integrable connection on the relative de Rham cohomology sheaves H^q_{DR}(X/S), the Gauss–Manin connection.
(9) Set K = Rf_*Ω•_{X/T}, a filtered complex on S.
(10) RΓ(S,K) ≅ RΓ(X,Ω•_{X/T}) = RH_DR(X/T).
(11) A 'general recipe' turns the filtered complex into a spectral sequence E_2^{pq} = H^p(S, α ↦ H^{α+q}(Gr^α K)), with differentials induced by d_1. In modern terms this is the hypercohomology spectral sequence for Deligne's décalée filtration: the E_1 term of Dec F is the hypercohomology of the complex of sheaves (E_1^{•,q}, d_1).
Combined with (3), on the next page this becomes the Katz–Oda 'Leray spectral sequence in de Rham cohomology', H^p_DR(S/T, H^q_DR(X/S)) ⇒ H^{p+q}_DR(X/T). Its intended use is to analyse classes in H^n_DR(X/T) whose image in H^0(S, H^n_DR(X/S)) vanishes (a horizontality / variation argument).

The whole page serves to define the Gauss–Manin connection algebraically and to relate it to Grothendieck's own (crystalline/infinitesimal) definition, which the previous page cites as 'celle que j'ai définie dans [ ]'.
errors: 'Ω^1_{S/T} plat sur S, i.e. S formellement lisse sur T' is wrong as an equivalence. Flatness (local freeness) of Ω^1 does not imply formal smoothness: for example S = Spec k[x]/(x^p) over a field k of characteristic p has Ω^1 free of rank 1 but is not smooth. For the purpose at hand only flatness of the Ω^p_{S/T} is needed, which Grothendieck himself notes on the next page ('il suffit Ω^1_{S/T} plat').
In (8) the tensor product should be derived (⊗^L), consistent with (6). This is notational only.

The 'recette générale' behind (11) is left implicit. It is valid (via décalage), but the identification of the d_1 maps with the Gauss–Manin maps needs the compatibility check flagged in the margin of p.162 ('il faut prouver une compatibilité de d_1 ...'). The projection formula in (3) is likewise admitted to be 'pas très catholique'.

ideas.what: Gauss–Manin connection as the d_1 of the Koszul filtration on Rf_*Ω•_{X/T}
ideas.modern_name: Katz–Oda construction of the Gauss–Manin connection
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's own definition is the crystalline one in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968); the Koszul-filtration construction appears in Katz–Oda, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 1968

ideas.what: Version for non-smooth S/T using derived tensor products Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω•_{X/S}, specializing to the classical connection when Ω^1_{S/T} is flat
ideas.modern_name: derived Gauss–Manin connection / Koszul filtration in derived de Rham theory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Oda (smooth case); later derived de Rham work of Illusie and Bhatt in a different form

ideas.what: Spectral sequence of a filtered complex with E_2 given by hypercohomology of the complex of E_1 sheaves; yields the Leray spectral sequence in de Rham cohomology H^p_DR(S/T, H^q_DR(X/S)) ⇒ H^{p+q}_DR(X/T)
ideas.modern_name: Katz–Oda Leray spectral sequence; Deligne décalage

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly wonders whether the Koszul-filtration connection coincides with his own crystalline definition, showing he was checking Katz–Oda's approach against his own. This is of historical interest only.
missed.quote: connexion de Gauss-Manin (Il semble bien que ce soit la même que celle que j'ai définie dans [ ] !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's reception of the Katz–Oda construction. The comparison itself is known in the literature (Katz, Berthelot–Ogus).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful re-derivation of the Katz–Oda construction and of the Leray spectral sequence in de Rham cohomology, both published in 1968. The slight generalization to non-flat Ω^1_{S/T} via derived tensor products is natural, is left unchecked, and contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: the crossed-out start reads approximately '[-Lorsque (X/S)-]' and is illegible beyond that; the inserted '(6)' above 'différentielles' matches the transcription.
In (8) the image shows a plain ⊗ (no L), though the derived tensor is meant.
'pour Ω^1_{S/T} plat sur S' — the image has 'Ω^1' (superscript 1 hard to read), consistent with the transcription.
